cards.text: Jesus just healed a man who was blind and mute, and the Pharisees said He drives out demons by Beelzebul (Matthew 12:22-24). Jesus answered them, and He did not hold back. Now some of the scribes, teachers of the law, step up with some Pharisees and call Him Teacher.

cards.question: The scribes and Pharisees just saw Jesus heal a blind and mute man. What do they ask Him for now?

cards.text: A SIGN. Friend, He just made a blind man SEE! That's like watching me pull a perfect batch out of the oven and saying, "Okay, but can you bake, though?"
Jesus answers them. He says a "wicked and adulterous generation demands a sign" and then He keeps going.

cards.question: Jesus tells the scribes and Pharisees that this generation will be given no sign at all.
Jesus says the one sign this generation will get is the sign of which prophet?

cards.text: Jonah, the prophet, ended up in the belly of a great fish. Jesus says as it was for Jonah, so it will be for the Son of Man, the name Jesus uses for Himself.

cards.question: How long does Jesus say Jonah was in the belly of the great fish?
Jesus says the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights too.

cards.text: Then Jesus brings up the men of Nineveh, the people Jonah preached to. He says they will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it.

cards.question: Why does Jesus say the men of Nineveh will condemn this generation at the judgment?

answers.text: They repented at the preaching of Jonah
They gave Jonah great gifts of silver
They sent Jonah back home in peace

cards.question: Nineveh repented when Jonah preached, and Jesus says now One ___ than Jonah is here.

cards.text: Nineveh listened to a prophet who'd been in the belly of a great fish, and they repented. Now Someone GREATER is standing right there... and these guys want a sign. Let that sit for a second.
Then Jesus names the Queen of the South, who came from the ends of the earth to hear a king. He says she will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it too.

cards.question: What did the Queen of the South come from the ends of the earth to hear?
Just like He said about Jonah, Jesus says One greater than Solomon is here.

cards.text: From the ENDS of the earth, friend. No GPS. No rest stops. She crossed all that for wisdom, and these guys have Someone greater than Solomon right in front of them, and they STILL want a sign.
Then Jesus tells what happens when an unclean spirit comes out of a man. It passes through arid places, seeking rest.

cards.question: The unclean spirit finds the rest it's looking for in the arid places.

cards.text: So the spirit makes a plan. It says, "I will return to the house I left."

cards.question: The unclean spirit goes back to the house it left. What does it find there?

cards.text: Vacant. Swept clean. Put in order. Nobody home. That's me deep-cleaning the WHOLE bakery and then leaving the front door wide open all night.

cards.question: The unclean spirit brings ___ other spirits more wicked than itself, and the man ends up ___ off than he was at first.
Jesus ends the picture of the unclean spirit by saying it will be the same with whom?

cards.text: While Jesus is still speaking to the crowds, His mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to speak to Him. Someone comes over and tells Him they're out there.

cards.question: Jesus hears His mother and brothers are outside, and He answers with a question. What does He ask?

answers.text: Who are My mother and brothers

cards.question: Jesus points and says, "Here are My mother and My brothers." Who is He pointing to?
Who does Jesus say is His brother and sister and mother?

answers.text: Whoever does the will of His Father
Whoever was born into His family
Whoever keeps every law of Moses

cards.text: Whoever does the will of His Father in heaven is family to Jesus. Trust me, friend, six little cookie cutters started calling me Papa, and not one of us was the same shape.

findings.problem: The Pharisees appear for the first time in the walkthrough, but the card never says who they are. The scribes get an intro ('teachers of the law'). The Pharisees don't.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: 'Jesus answered them, and He did not hold back' is a Bible fact from Matthew 12:25-37. It has no reference, because the inline reference only covers Matthew 12:22-24.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The card tells context from the previous passage (Matthew 12:22-24) with an inline reference, but its verses field is only Matthew 12:38.
findings.question: When a story card uses context from outside the passage and gives it an inline reference, should the card's verses field include those outside verses, or only the passage verses it tells?

findings.problem: The question says the scribes and Pharisees 'just saw Jesus heal a blind and mute man.' Matthew 12:24 says the Pharisees heard about it ('when the Pharisees heard this'), and the scribes aren't mentioned there at all. The text shows that 'saw' is wrong.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: This story card only reacts to the request for a sign from card 2. It tells no new part of the passage. Its joke should ride along on a card that moves the passage forward. It also states the healing as a Bible fact ('He just made a blind man SEE') with no reference.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This is a recap card. It restates Matthew 12:41, which cards 10 to 12 already covered, and tells nothing new. It also uses Jonah being in the belly of the great fish (Matthew 12:40) but cites only Matthew 12:41.
The Queen of the South appears for the first time with no simple intro to who she is. Solomon is never introduced either (for example, as Israel's king) when he comes up on cards 15 and 16.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This is a recap card. It restates Matthew 12:42 and the 'they still want a sign' point that card 13 already made, and it moves the passage nowhere.

This card mostly recaps the answer to card 4 (vacant, swept clean). Its joke about leaving the front door wide open all night also hints that something worse is coming in. That points toward 'worse' on card 6 and rules out 'better.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card opens by recapping card 11's answer. The joke compares Jesus' family with cookie cutters that are 'not the same shape,' so it is about being different. But Matthew 12:50 is about doing the Father's will, so the comparison doesn't share the same core action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
